title: Nightshift triage: ECC spike and driver hangs on GPU nodes
content:
Summary:

This doc is a nightshift on-call triage log and preliminary runbook draft for a recurring pattern observed on a subset of GPU nodes in cluster prod-gpu-1: short bursts of ECC single-bit errors followed within ~30–90s by increased NVLink RTT and ultimately a driver hang (nvidia driver watchdog) that leads to a kernel panic on the host. Incident windows observed 2025-09-28 -> 2025-10-03 across nodes gpu-node-11, gpu-node-18, gpu-node-22. This file records what we observed, immediate mitigations used during the night shift, commands and checklists for oncall, and proposed follow-ups (short and mid-term).

Why this doc exists: to consolidate nightshift knowledge (messy logs, partial hypotheses) into a reproducible triage flow and temporary mitigations while engineering drives a long-term fix.

Immediate timeline (selected events):
- 2025-09-28 02:41 UTC: alert ECC-rate-high triggered for gpu-node-11 (single-bit ECC count increased > 120 in 5m).
- 2025-09-28 02:42 UTC: nvlink-latency-alert fired for the same host (avg NVLink RTT > baseline + 4x)
- 2025-09-28 02:43 UTC: processes using GPU on node report CUDA_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE errors; jobs auto-evicted by kubelet.
- 2025-09-28 02:44 UTC: driver watchdog triggered; host kernel Oops and panic at 02:46. Node went down, SRE page invoked.
- 2025-10-01 05:18 UTC: similar pattern on gpu-node-18; node recovered after manual power-cycle of PCIe riser after hardware team intervention.
- 2025-10-03 03:09 UTC: repeated short ECC spikes on gpu-node-22 followed by transient nvlink errors; automated drain succeeded, no panic (different driver minor revision present).

Observed signals and telemetry (what we saw):
- nvidia-smi pmon / dmon showed ECC single-bit counters rising quickly on a single GPU on node (e.g., GPU0).
- dmesg/journalctl showed nvlink link flaps and repeated "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:XX:00:00): 31" style errors preceding driver recoveries. Xid codes included 31 and 62 in different incidents.
- pmc and host telemetry showed NVLink latency spikes concurrent with ECC bursts.
- firmware versions: some affected nodes running GPU firmware 2.14.1, others (less affected) running 2.13.6. Driver versions varied between 535.86 and 541.09.
- PCIe topology: affected GPUs often had dual NVLink bridges to adjacent GPUs; several have been in service since 2023 without prior firmware refresh.

Quick triage checklist for oncall (run this first):
1) Verify alert sources and scope: check ECC-rate, nvlink-latency, and driver-hang alerts in Grafana. Note which GPU index and host.
2) Run quick health checks (commands):
   - ssh to host (prefer bastion), sudo -i
   - nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTILIZATION
   - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,serial,firmware,driver_model --format=csv
   - journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service -n 200 --no-pager || journalctl -k -b --no-pager | grep -i nvrm
   - sudo cat /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/ports/1/mtu (NVLink datapath checks on hosts with NVSwitch overlay)
   - ipmitool chassis power status (if suspect power glitch)
3) If ECC single-bit count is rising rapidly (>50/s sustained) and NVLink latency alerts present:
   - Immediately cordon and drain node (kubectl cordon node && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data) to prevent running jobs from hitting driver hang.
   - If jobs already failing due to CUDA_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE, escalate to Page if nodes show kernel Oops pattern.
4) Avoid restarting the nvidia driver in-situ if kernel panic imminent. If driver unresponsive but node still responsive, collect diagnostics and consider live-reboot only after drain.

Temporary mitigations used during nightshift (what we did):
- For gpu-node-11 we drained and power-cycled the node via BMC after collecting logs (dmesg, nvidia-smi -q). Power-cycle returned node to healthy state and ECC counters did not climb post-boot.
- For gpu-node-18 the hardware team removed and reseated an NVLink bridge and replaced a suspect PCIe riser. That node showed no further ECC spikes for 48h.
- For gpu-node-22 we used an automated drain policy (scale down of GPU workloads) when NVLink RTT exceeded threshold; that prevented panic but did not address root cause.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) NVLink hardware/bridge degradation combined with firmware-driver mismatch: ECC bursts are symptomatic of link errors; when bursts exceed a threshold driver routines become stressed and lead to unrecoverable Xid errors and watchdog timeouts. Evidence: reseating bridge resolved a node; nodes with older firmware showed more frequent recurrences.
2) Power delivery instability to GPU rails under certain workloads leads to increased bit flips (ECC), link retries, and eventual driver timeouts. Evidence: ipmi logs on one host showed power transient around incident time.
3) Driver regression in 541.x interacting badly with firmware 2.14.y: some nodes on 541.09 saw panics while others on 535.86 only had transient recoveries.

Commands and snippets we found useful (copyable):
- Snapshot ECC + util: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,clocks.current.graphics,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv -l 1
- Persistent ECC totals: for g in $(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index --format=csv,noheader); do nvidia-smi --id=$g --query-ecc-errors=volatile.single_bit,volatile.double_bit --format=csv; done
- Dump Xid entries: journalctl -k -b --no-pager | grep -i "NVRM: Xid" | tail -n 200
- NVLink counters (where supported): nvidia-smi nvlink -q && nvidia-smi nvlink --query -i 0,1 --format=csv

Runbook draft (short):
- Alert -> run checklist -> drain -> collect logs -> power-cycle if hardware suspected -> escalate to hardware-team for physical inspection -> ticket owner creates hardware replacement/firmware plan.
- Add automated pre-drain if ECC single-bit > 200 in 2 minutes OR NVLink RTT > baseline + 5x for 1 minute.

Open follow-ups (owners + rough prioritization):
- INFRA-2104 (Owner: Priya Rao) - Investigate firmware/driver correlation across fleet; produce matrix of GPU firmware vs driver version vs incident rate. Priority: P0.
- INFRA-2107 (Owner: Diego Martinez) - Add NVLink and ECC burst synthetic test to nightly hardware health check (run worst-case memory+nvlink stress test for 2h). Priority: P1.
- INFRA-2112 (Owner: Hardware Team / Ethan Cho) - Replace NVLink bridges on nodes with >3 incidents in last 90d and audit PCIe riser power connectors. Priority: P1.
- INFRA-2120 (Owner: eng-serving-runtime) - Add graceful fallback in runtime to avoid kernel watchdog when Xid 31/62 detected: throttle requests, flush caches, reduce concurrency. Priority: P2.

Instrumentation and alert tuning notes:
- Current ECC alert threshold is static (50/min). This produces a noisy signal during aggressive stress tests; proposal: change to two-level alert: warning 50/min, critical 200/min. Add rolling-window smoothing (exponential).
- Add an NVLink RTT baseline per topology (two adjacent GPUs, ring vs pair) instead of global baseline.

Repro attempts (what we tried in lab):
- Reproduced ECC bursts on a staging node by running memory-rw + nvlink-stress from CUDA samples for ~45m; observed single-bit rates similar to prod and intermittent nvlink link loss.
- Reproduced driver hang only when combining an older firmware image with newer driver (541.x) and stressing NVLink heavily for >1h. On lab machines, downgrading driver to 535.86 avoided the hang but did not eliminate ECC.

Post-incident retrospective notes (what to discuss in retro):
- Hardware replacement cadence: should we proactively replace NVLink bridges older than N months?
- Firmware rollout policy: ensure driver+firmware matrix validation before fleet upgrades.
- Automated node isolation: current automated drain prevented some panics but hardware teams still had manual work — can we accelerate the path from alert to BMC power-cycle while preserving logs?

Appendix A — Quick checklist for hardware team arrival:
- Collect /var/log/messages and journalctl -k -b (save full output).
- Preserve GPU firmware images (nvidia-smi -q) and serial numbers.
- Visually inspect NVLink bridge seating and PCIe risers; reseat and torque to spec.
- Replace NVLink bridge if visible wear or repeated incidents.
- Note ambient temperatures and rack power usage around incident times.

Appendix B — Helpful links and internal references:
- Confluence: INFRA-2104 (driver/firmware matrix)
- Slack: #sre-nightshift (thread around 2025-10-03)
- Jira: INFRA-2107, INFRA-2112, INFRA-2120

Notes to self (messy):
- We should capture nvlink counters at 1s granularity when an ECC spike starts — currently dashboards at 10s mask short flaps.
- Consider enabling QDR-like link margin logging on GPUs (if supported) to detect degraded lanes before ECC bursts.
- Keep an eye on PSU logs for the cluster — two incidents had correlated BMC power complaints.

If you're reading this while oncall: use the triage checklist, don't try to hot-patch drivers on a live node unless hardware confirms it's safe, and escalate to page when kernel Oops/panic patterns appear.

-- Maya (nightshift oncall)
